records.reported_shipment: Containers aboard OOCL Sunflower on a voyage from Taiwan to Long Beach, California
records.reported_carrier: Orient Overseas Container Line (reported vessel operator)
records.location: North Pacific, south of the Aleutian Island chain
records.reported_loss_or_damage: NOAA's initial notification reported 32 containers lost overboard. A separate Safety4Sea account reported 57. W.K. Webster later reported at least 32 lost, additional containers damaged or shifted, and removal operations beginning after the vessel arrived in Long Beach on 18 March; the final count and container contents are not verified.

source.publisher: United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise factual summary and link only.

limitations: NOAA's initial notification dated 9 March reported 32 lost containers, while https://safety4sea.com/vessel-loses-57-containers-overboard-on-route-to-long-beach/ reported 57; no final reconciled count was located.
The arrival and removal operations are reported by W.K. Webster at https://wkwebster.com/casualties/738/oocl-sunflower; their report does not establish when removal or cargo recovery was completed.
Neither reviewed report confirms the contents, shipment owners, cargo value, or final recovery and damage assessment. Container loss does not by itself establish the loss of goods.
The precise incident jurisdiction is unverified. Taiwan and the United States are voyage endpoints, not assumed incident location or supplier impact.
The operator is not necessarily the contractual carrier for any individual shipment. No case-study shipment has been matched.

search_window.note: Spans the loss date and the later reported arrival and commencement of container removal; not proof of continuous disruption or completion of recovery. Search end also includes the illustrative maximum handling-delay scenario; it is not an observed recovery date.

scenario_recovery.scope: hypothetical handling delay after reported container-removal operations began, not from incident date
scenario_recovery.basis: illustrative uncalibrated scenario; severity is a subjective handling assumption, not a measured incident severity

records.incident_type: vessel sinking and reported containers overboard
records.reported_shipment: 107 containers reported aboard Golden Star 1 on a Singapore-to-Malaysia voyage
records.location: Singapore Strait, approximately 6 km off Batam, Indonesia
records.reported_loss_or_damage: Singapore's maritime authority reported the sinking and warned vessels to report containers adrift. Xinde Marine News reported that all 107 containers aboard entered the sea; Baird Maritime reported that some were found the following morning. The number lost and container contents were not confirmed by the authority's reviewed statement.

source.publisher: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise factual summary and link only.

limitations: The reported location is off Indonesia, outside the six study countries; this contextual record is included because the reported voyage connected Singapore and Malaysia.

The claim that 107 containers went overboard and the Singapore-to-Pasir Gudang voyage are from https://www.xindemarinenews.com/news/2063910861887766529; the official statement does not confirm the number or voyage endpoints.
The Straits Times separately reported 107 containers aboard citing Antara, not that all were lost: https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/tanzania-registered-container-vessel-sinks-off-batam.

Baird Maritime reported that some containers were found on 6 June: https://www.bairdmaritime.com/security/incidents/accidents/containership-sinks-off-batam-indonesia-all-on-board-rescued. Finding containers does not establish cargo recovery or a completion date.
Container contents, recovery, cargo damage, carrier contracts, and case-study shipment impact are unknown. The MPA said vessel traffic remained unaffected at the time of its statement.

search_window.note: Spans the reported sinking and discovery of some containers the following morning; cargo recovery and assessment completion are unknown. Search end also includes the illustrative maximum handling-delay scenario; it is not an observed recovery date.

scenario_recovery.scope: hypothetical initial cargo handling disruption, not navigational closure or total cargo recovery
scenario_recovery.basis: illustrative uncalibrated scenario; severity is a subjective handling assumption, not a measured incident severity
